items.title: 3 Boring Businesses That Keep Customers Coming Back and Profits Growing
items.summary: A vending machine bolted to a factory floor can lock in a customer for years. Three unglamorous distributors have mastered that trick, and one of them still turned a $0.25 dividend into a decade-long wealth machine for patient owners.

items.title: Fastenal Stock Is Up 35% in 2026. Is Its Dividend Still Worth Buying?
items.summary: Fastenal's shares have surged, and the yield has shrunk along with it. Retirees counting on that quarterly check should look at what the payout depends on, and at one slowdown in factory orders that deserves a close watch.

items.title: IBD Stock Of The Day Grainger Surges On Best Revenue Growth In 5 Years
items.summary: IBD's Stock Of The Day, W.W. Grainger, shot up about 8% on Wednesday after handily beating earnings.

items.title: W.W. Grainger Earnings Ahead: What Past Reactions Say About The Stock
items.summary: W.W. Grainger (NYSE:GWW) is scheduled to report its earnings on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. The company has a market value of about $65.0 billion. Over the last twelve months it generated $18.8 billion in revenue and $2.7 billion in operating profit, with net income of $1.9 billion.

items.title: ETFs Are Net Sellers of Fastenal (FAST) on Oct. 30
items.summary: ETFs sold a net $50.9 million of Fastenal (FAST) shares last Friday.

items.title: Rollins Has Grown Revenue for 100 Straight Quarters. Here Are 3 More Boring Businesses to Watch
items.summary: Rollins just logged a milestone that spans two crashes and a pandemic, and three other unglamorous businesses share the same stubborn habit of growing no matter what the economy does.

items.title: EBay Leads Five Stocks Near Buy Points From Resilient Sectors
items.summary: Ebay, Quest Diagnostics, Fastenal, Chubb trade in or around buy points after earnings. TG Therapeutics breaks out.

items.title: 2 large-cap stocks with impressive fundamentals and 1 we ignore
items.summary: Large-cap stocks usually command their industries because they have the scale to drive market trends. The flip side though is that their sheer size can limit growth as expanding further becomes an increasingly challenging task.
